lab_questions.title: Timezone-Aware Scheduling
lab_questions.description: Doctors create availability slots in their local timezone. Patients book them from different timezones. The application currently stores everything as naive datetime strings.
lab_questions.startup_command: python manage.py migrate && python manage.py runserver 0.0.0.0:8010

tasks.title: UTC Normalization
tasks.description:
The POST /api/doctors/availability/ endpoint saves naive datetimes. Patients booking slots are off by hours.

**Goal:** Ensure all incoming scheduling data is coerced to timezone-aware UTC using Python utilities before database saving. The output GET API must serialize these back out with proper ISO-8601 offset strings.

tasks.title: Prevent Double Booking
tasks.description:
Doctors should not be able to create overlapping availability slots. Since slots can be created from different timezones, naive overlap checks can fail.

**Goal:** Add a `validate()` method to the serializer that queries the database for existing slots for the same `doctor_name`. If the proposed slot overlaps with an existing slot (i.e. starts before the existing slot ends AND ends after the existing slot starts), raise a `serializers.ValidationError({"non_field_errors": "Overlapping slot"})`.

tasks.title: Maximum Slot Duration
tasks.description:
A single availability slot must not exceed 8 real-world hours. Because a slot might cross a Daylight Saving Time (DST) transition boundary, naive math might be inaccurate.

**Goal:** Validate that the duration between `start_time` and `end_time` is strictly 8 hours or less. Use the UTC-aware datetimes to calculate this true duration. Raise a `serializers.ValidationError({"non_field_errors": "Duration exceeds 8 hours"})` if it fails.
